subject: Clarification: end-of-period timestamps and sampling cutoff for SOC 2 evidence

Subject: Clarification: end-of-period timestamps and sampling cutoff for SOC 2 evidence

Hi Laura,

Hope you are well. We're prepping the SOC 2 evidence package for Acme Cloud and have a question about how your audit team treats "end-of-period" timestamps and point-in-time samples. Our reporting period on the current Type II report covers 2025-06-01 through 2026-05-31. A couple of specifics we want to confirm so we can assemble the correct extracts: 

- Does your team treat the audit period as inclusive of the full end date (i.e., 2026-05-31 23:59:59) or do you operate on a strict <date-only> boundary? We record system events in UTC with second-level precision.
- For controls that are validated via point-in-time artifacts (for example: configuration snapshots, access-control manifests, and token revocation lists), do you accept system-produced UTC timestamps as primary evidence? If an evidence item was taken at 2026-06-01T00:00:03Z due to collection timing, would that fall outside the period?
- If there is a small extraction window that spills a few seconds/minutes past the nominal cutoff, is a bridge letter acceptable to reconcile that gap, and if so, what language / attestations do you expect?

We've attached the current Type II report PDF and a draft bridge letter so you can review. If it's easier, happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2025-06-01_2026-05-31.pdf, bridge_letter_template_v1.docx

From: Laura Stevens <laura.stevens@primeaudit.com>

Subject: Re: Clarification: end-of-period timestamps and sampling cutoff for SOC 2 evidence

Hi Irene — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers first, followed by a recommended approach.

1) Inclusivity of end date: We treat the audit period as inclusive of the full end date. For your example that means artifacts timestamped up to and including 2026-05-31 23:59:59 UTC are squarely in-period. Anything with a timestamp of 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z or later is considered outside the period. Our reports use UTC for consistency.

2) Point-in-time evidence: We accept system-produced UTC timestamps as primary evidence provided the system clock is authenticated and there is a clear provenance chain (log entries, checksum/manifest, or signed attestations). For items collected very close to the cutoff (e.g., a snapshot taken at 2026-06-01T00:00:03Z because the snapshot job runs just after midnight), that exact file would be outside the covered period. However, we evaluate the control test as a whole — if you can show that the snapshot process is deterministic and include the previous in-period snapshot plus an attestation explaining the collection timing, we can accept that as complementary evidence.

3) Bridge letters: Yes, a bridge letter is an acceptable remediation when the evidence slightly spills over. Key elements we need in the bridge letter:
   - Exact statement of the gap (dates/times and why the spill occurred).
   - Who is attesting (title and name) and that they have direct knowledge of the systems/processes.
   - A description of compensating controls or why the late artifact does not materially affect the control assertion (for example, deterministic snapshots, immutability of logs, or multiple overlapping artifacts).
   - A signature and date.

I've attached a short template that our engagement team uses — it calls out the minimum attestations above. If you prefer, we can redline your draft instead. Also note: for automated evidence (logs/metrics), include a manifest (CSV) with filename, UTC timestamp, SHA256, and extraction query so we can map samples to source data quickly.

Cheers,
Laura Stevens
Senior IT Audit Manager
PrimeAudit Partners

Attachments: bridge_letter_template_v1.docx (attached), sample_bridge_language.txt (inline)
